-- A turn-based terminal game. Run with:
--   cabal run emlf -- --run examples/snake.emlf
-- Type w/a/s/d and Enter to move, Enter alone to continue, or q to quit.
-- Monad and its IO instance come from the standard prelude.

data List a = Nil | Cons a (List a)
data Maybe a = Nothing | Just a
data Position = Position Int Int
data Direction = North | South | West | East
data Command = Turn Direction | Forward | Quit | Invalid
-- A snake always has a head; its body may be empty.
data Snake = Snake Position (List Position)
data Game = Game Snake Direction Position Int
data Outcome = Continue Game | Lost String Int | Won Int

width = 12
height = 8

samePosition (Position x y) (Position x' y') = x == x' && y == y'

contains : Position -> List Position -> Bool
contains position Nil = false
contains position (Cons first rest) =
  samePosition position first || contains position rest

dropLast : forall a. List a -> List a
dropLast Nil = Nil
dropLast (Cons _ Nil) = Nil
dropLast (Cons first rest) = Cons first (dropLast rest)

move direction (Position x y) =
  case direction of
    North -> Position x (y - 1)
    South -> Position x (y + 1)
    West -> Position (x - 1) y
    East -> Position (x + 1) y

opposite North South = true
opposite South North = true
opposite West East = true
opposite East West = true
opposite _ _ = false

outside (Position x y) =
  x < 0 || y < 0 || x == width || y == height

-- Food is deterministic: scan from the top left for the first free square.
-- Reaching the bottom means the board is full, so the player has won.
findFood : List Position -> Maybe Position
findFood occupied =
  let rec
    scan : Int -> Int -> Maybe Position
    scan x y =
      if y == height then Nothing
      else if x == width then scan 0 (y + 1)
      else let candidate = Position x y in
        if contains candidate occupied then scan (x + 1) y
        else Just candidate
  in scan 0 0

step : Direction -> Game -> Outcome
step requested (Game (Snake head body) heading food score) =
  let
    -- Reversing is ignored, but the turn still advances one square.
    direction = if opposite heading requested then heading else requested
    next = move direction head
    eating = samePosition next food
    -- On an ordinary move the old tail leaves before collision checking.
    remaining = if eating then Cons head body else dropLast (Cons head body)
    moved = Snake next remaining
  in
    if outside next then Lost "wall" score
    else if contains next remaining then Lost "body" score
    else if eating then
      let newScore = score + 1 in
      case findFood (Cons next remaining) of
        Nothing -> Won newScore
        Just newFood -> Continue (Game moved direction newFood newScore)
    else Continue (Game moved direction food score)

parseCommand "q" = Quit
parseCommand "w" = Turn North
parseCommand "s" = Turn South
parseCommand "a" = Turn West
parseCommand "d" = Turn East
parseCommand "" = Forward
parseCommand _ = Invalid

tile (Game (Snake head body) _ food _) position =
  if samePosition position head then "@"
  else if contains position body then "o"
  else if samePosition position food then "*"
  else "."

row : Game -> Int -> String
row game y =
  let rec
    cells : Int -> String
    cells x =
      if x == width then "|\n"
      else tile game (Position x y) ++ cells (x + 1)
  in "|" ++ cells 0

rows : Game -> Int -> String
rows game y =
  if y == height then ""
  else row game y ++ rows game (y + 1)

directionName North = "up"
directionName South = "down"
directionName West = "left"
directionName East = "right"

draw : Game -> IO ()
draw game =
  case game of
    Game _ heading _ score -> do
      putStrLn ("\nScore: " ++ showInt score ++ "  Direction: " ++ directionName heading)
      putStrLn "+------------+"
      putStr (rows game 0)
      putStrLn "+------------+"

play : Game -> IO ()
play game = do
  draw game
  putStr "Move [w/a/s/d, Enter, q]: "
  input <- getLine
  case game of
    Game _ heading _ score ->
      let
        advance direction =
          case step direction game of
            Continue next -> play next
            Lost reason finalScore ->
              putStrLn ("Game over: hit " ++ reason ++ ". Score: " ++ showInt finalScore)
            Won finalScore ->
              putStrLn ("You filled the board! Score: " ++ showInt finalScore)
      in case parseCommand input of
        Quit -> putStrLn ("Goodbye. Score: " ++ showInt score)
        Invalid -> do
          putStrLn "Use w, a, s, d, Enter, or q. No move made."
          play game
        Forward -> advance heading
        Turn direction -> advance direction

initial = Game
  (Snake (Position 4 3) (Cons (Position 3 3) (Cons (Position 2 3) Nil)))
  East (Position 6 3) 0

main = do
  putStrLn "Snake: @ head, o body, * food. The board is 12 by 8."
  putStrLn "WASD + Enter moves; Enter continues; q quits. Reverse turns are ignored."
  putStrLn "Eat food to grow. Avoid walls and your body. Food uses the first free square."
  play initial

-- Benchmarks Game binary-trees, translated for this repository.
-- Read the maximum depth from stdin. See ../PROVENANCE.md.
-- Every leaf is a full Node with two Nil fields, like an interior node.

data Tree = Nil | Node Tree Tree

-- Retain the bounded decimal input parser used by the original benchmark.
readDepth : String -> Int
readDepth text =
  let rec
    search : Int -> Int
    search n = if eqString text (showInt n) then n else if n == 20 then 0 else search (n + 1)
  in search 0

power2 : Int -> Int
power2 n =
  if n == 0 then 1
  else
    let
      half = power2 (n - 1)
    in half + half

-- Force both child roots before returning Node, recursively constructing
-- every node. Keep the actual children; do not rebuild or share subtrees.
make : Int -> Tree
make depth =
  if depth == 0 then Node Nil Nil
  else
    let
      left = make (depth - 1)
    in case left of
      Nil -> Nil
      Node _ _ ->
        let
          right = make (depth - 1)
        in case right of
          Nil -> Nil
          Node _ _ -> Node left right

check : Tree -> Int
check Nil = 0
check (Node left right) = 1 + (check left + check right)

line label depth count = putStrLn (label ++ " of depth " ++ showInt depth ++ "\t check: " ++ showInt count)

-- Force the accumulated check before the next IO action. Each iteration
-- gives the collector a safe point, releasing that tree; lazy counts would
-- otherwise retain every completed tree until output.
sumTrees : Int -> Int -> Int -> IO Int
sumTrees depth remaining total =
  if remaining == 0 then return total
  else
    let
      next = total + check (make depth)
    in if next == next then do
      forced <- return next
      sumTrees depth (remaining - 1) forced
    else return 0

depths : Int -> Int -> IO ()
depths maximum depth =
  if maximum < depth then return ()
  else
    let
      iterations = power2 (maximum - depth + 4)
    in do
      total <- sumTrees depth iterations 0
      line (showInt iterations ++ "\t trees") depth total
      depths maximum (depth + 2)

main = do
  input <- getLine
  let
    requested = readDepth input
    maximum = if requested < 6 then 6 else requested
  in do
    line "stretch tree" (maximum + 1) (check (make (maximum + 1)))
    let
      long = make maximum
    in case long of
      Nil -> putStrLn "invalid tree"
      Node _ _ -> do
        depths maximum 4
        line "long lived tree" maximum (check long)

-- Incremental permutation/count arrays and a separate flip workspace.
-- No permutation or flip operation is delegated to the native runtime.

data Result = Result Int Int

initialize : IntArray -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
initialize perm n i =
  if i == n then return ()
  else do
    writeIntArray perm i (i + 1)
    initialize perm n (i + 1)

copy : IntArray -> IntArray -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
copy source dest n i =
  if i == n then return ()
  else do
    x <- readIntArray source i
    writeIntArray dest i x
    copy source dest n (i + 1)

reversePrefix : IntArray -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
reversePrefix perm i j =
  if i < j then do
    x <- readIntArray perm i
    y <- readIntArray perm j
    writeIntArray perm i y
    writeIntArray perm j x
    reversePrefix perm (i + 1) (j - 1)
  else return ()

countFlips : IntArray -> Int -> IO Int
countFlips perm flips = do
  first <- readIntArray perm 0
  if first == 1 then return flips
  else do
    reversePrefix perm 0 (first - 1)
    countFlips perm (flips + 1)

rotate : IntArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
rotate perm end first i =
  if i == end then writeIntArray perm end first
  else do
    x <- readIntArray perm (i + 1)
    writeIntArray perm i x
    rotate perm end first (i + 1)

nextPermutation : IntArray -> IntArray -> Int -> Int -> IO Bool
nextPermutation perm count n i =
  if i == n then return false
  else do
    first <- readIntArray perm 0
    rotate perm i first 0
    c <- readIntArray count i
    if c < i then do
      writeIntArray count i (c + 1)
      return true
    else do
      writeIntArray count i 0
      nextPermutation perm count n (i + 1)

-- Demand both accumulators before the next action, as binary-trees does.
-- Otherwise a lazy chain retains all completed permutations until output.
permutations : IntArray -> IntArray -> IntArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO Result
permutations perm scratch count n index checksum maximum = do
  copy perm scratch n 0
  flips <- countFlips scratch 0
  let total = if index % 2 == 0 then checksum + flips else checksum - flips
  let best = if maximum < flips then flips else maximum
  if total == total then
    if best == best then do
      more <- nextPermutation perm count n 1
      if more then permutations perm scratch count n (index + 1) total best else return (Result total best)
    else return (Result 0 0)
  else return (Result 0 0)

main = do
  input <- getLine
  let n = readInt input
  perm <- newIntArray n 0
  scratch <- newIntArray n 0
  count <- newIntArray n 0
  initialize perm n 0
  result <- permutations perm scratch count n 0 0 0
  case result of
    Result checksum maximum -> do
      printInt checksum
      putStrLn ("Pfannkuchen(" ++ showInt n ++ ") = " ++ showInt maximum)

-- Copy ALU, then generate both random sequences with one continuous LCG.
-- General byte arrays buffer 1024 complete 60-column lines per output action.

minimum a b = if a < b then a else b

chunkBytes n = n + (n + 59) / 60

cumulative : DoubleArray -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
cumulative probabilities length i =
  if i < length then do
    previous <- readDoubleArray probabilities (i - 1)
    current <- readDoubleArray probabilities i
    writeDoubleArray probabilities i (addDouble previous current)
    cumulative probabilities length (i + 1)
  else return ()

search : ByteArray -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> Int -> Int -> IO Int
search alphabet probabilities random lo hi =
  if lo + 1 < hi then do
    let middle = (lo + hi) / 2
    p <- readDoubleArray probabilities middle
    r <- readDoubleArray random 0
    if ltDouble r p then search alphabet probabilities random lo middle
    else search alphabet probabilities random middle hi
  else readByteArray alphabet hi

select alphabet probabilities random length = do
  p <- readDoubleArray probabilities 0
  r <- readDoubleArray random 0
  if ltDouble r p then readByteArray alphabet 0 else search alphabet probabilities random 0 (length - 1)

-- Force the changing counters at saturation to keep loop arguments
-- evaluated without changing any output work.
repeatFill : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO Int
repeatFill source out length count i index column offset =
  let
    counters = i + (index + (column + offset))
  in if counters == counters then
    if column == 60 then do
      writeByteArray out offset 10
      repeatFill source out length count i index 0 (offset + 1)
    else
      if i == count then
        if column == 0 then return index
        else do
          writeByteArray out offset 10
          return index
      else do
        byte <- readByteArray source index
        writeByteArray out offset byte
        let next = if index + 1 < length then index + 1 else 0
        repeatFill source out length count (i + 1) next (column + 1) (offset + 1)
  else return 0

repeatChunks : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
repeatChunks source out length remaining index =
  if remaining == 0 then return ()
  else do
    let count = minimum remaining 61440
    next <- repeatFill source out length count 0 index 0 0
    putBytes out 0 (chunkBytes count)
    repeatChunks source out length (remaining - count) next

randomFill : ByteArray -> DoubleArray -> IntArray -> DoubleArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
randomFill alphabet probabilities seed random out length count i column offset =
  let
    counters = i + (column + offset)
  in if counters == counters then
    if column == 60 then do
      writeByteArray out offset 10
      randomFill alphabet probabilities seed random out length count i 0 (offset + 1)
    else
      if i == count then if column == 0 then return () else writeByteArray out offset 10
      else do
        previous <- readIntArray seed 0
        let next = (previous * 3877 + 29573) % 139968
        writeIntArray seed 0 next
        writeDoubleArray random 0 (divDouble (intToDouble next) 139968.0)
        byte <- select alphabet probabilities random length
        writeByteArray out offset byte
        randomFill alphabet probabilities seed random out length count (i + 1) (column + 1) (offset + 1)
  else return ()

randomChunks : ByteArray -> DoubleArray -> IntArray -> DoubleArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
randomChunks alphabet probabilities seed random out length remaining =
  if remaining == 0 then return ()
  else do
    let count = minimum remaining 61440
    randomFill alphabet probabilities seed random out length count 0 0 0
    putBytes out 0 (chunkBytes count)
    randomChunks alphabet probabilities seed random out length (remaining - count)

  let n = readInt input

  iub <- byteArrayFromString "acgtBDHKMNRSVWY"
  homo <- byteArrayFromString "acgt"
  iubProb <- newDoubleArray 15 0.02
  writeDoubleArray iubProb 0 0.27
  writeDoubleArray iubProb 1 0.12
  writeDoubleArray iubProb 2 0.12
  writeDoubleArray iubProb 3 0.27

  writeDoubleArray homoProb 1 0.1979883004921
  writeDoubleArray homoProb 2 0.1975473066391

-- Full k-mer frequency tables for lengths 1,2,3,4,6,12,18.
-- Keys use the permitted base-4 encoding; every overlapping substring is
-- looked up and updated in a general, library-backed IntTable.

data Buffer = Buffer ByteArray Int Int

minimum a b = if a < b then a else b

-- Read one line at a time. Each record starts small and doubles as needed;
-- no file-size query or whole-input allocation is used.
copy : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
copy source dest n offset i =
  if i < n then do
    b <- readByteArray source i
    writeByteArray dest (offset + i) b
    copy source dest n offset (i + 1)
  else return ()

capacityFor : Int -> Int -> IO Int
capacityFor capacity needed = if capacity < needed then capacityFor (capacity * 2) needed else return capacity

trimLine : ByteArray -> Int -> IO Int
trimLine line n =
  if n == 0 then return 0
  else do
    b <- readByteArray line (n - 1)
    if b == 10 then trimLine line (n - 1) else if b == 13 then trimLine line (n - 1) else return n

isThree : ByteArray -> Int -> IO Bool
isThree line length =
  if length < 6 then return false
  else do
    a <- readByteArray line 0
    b <- readByteArray line 1
    c <- readByteArray line 2
    d <- readByteArray line 3
    e <- readByteArray line 4
    f <- readByteArray line 5
    let prefix = a == 62 && b == 84 && c == 72 && d == 82 && e == 69 && f == 69
    if prefix then
      if length == 6 then return true
      else do
        next <- readByteArray line 6
        return (next == 32 || next == 9 || next == 10 || next == 13)
    else return false

code 65 = 0
code 97 = 0
code 67 = 1
code 99 = 1
code 71 = 2
code 103 = 2
code _ = 3

-- Decode each input base once; growth copies preserve these numeric bytes.
decodeLine : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
decodeLine line bytes count offset i =
  if i < count then do
    b <- readByteArray line i
    writeByteArray bytes (offset + i) (code b)
    decodeLine line bytes count offset (i + 1)
  else return ()

skip : () -> IO ()
skip unused = do
  line <- getByteLine
  n <- lengthByteArray line
  if n == 0 then return ()
  else do
    found <- isThree line n
    if found then return () else skip ()

readSequence : ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> IO Buffer
readSequence bytes used capacity = do
  line <- getByteLine
  n <- lengthByteArray line
  if n == 0 then return (Buffer bytes used capacity)
  else do
    first <- readByteArray line 0
    if first == 62 then return (Buffer bytes used capacity)
    else do
      count <- trimLine line n
      let needed = used + count
      if capacity < needed then do
        next <- capacityFor capacity needed
        grown <- newByteArray next 0
        copy bytes grown used 0 0
        decodeLine line grown count used 0
        readSequence grown needed next
      else do
        decodeLine line bytes count used 0
        readSequence bytes needed capacity

encode : ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO Int
encode bytes i end key =
  if i < end then do
    b <- readByteArray bytes i
    encode bytes (i + 1) end (key * 4 + code b)
  else return key

prefix : ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO Int
prefix bytes i end key =
  if i < end then do
    b <- readByteArray bytes i
    prefix bytes (i + 1) end (key * 4 + b)
  else return key

power4 : Int -> Int -> IO Int
power4 n value = if n == 0 then return value else power4 (n - 1) (value * 4)

-- Maintain a base-4 sliding window, masking off its outgoing digit before
-- appending the next. Every window updates the complete frequency table.
countFrame : ByteArray -> IntTable -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
countFrame bytes table length k mask start key = do
  old <- readIntTable table key
  writeIntTable table key (old + 1)
  let next = start + k
  if next < length then do
    incoming <- readByteArray bytes next
    let rolled = andInt (key * 4) mask + incoming
    countFrame bytes table length k mask (start + 1) rolled
  else return ()

count : ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> IO IntTable
count bytes length k = do
  table <- newIntTable
  if length < k then return ()
  else do
    key <- prefix bytes 0 k 0
    limit <- power4 k 1
    countFrame bytes table length k (limit - 1) 0 key
  return table

letter 0 = "A"
letter 1 = "C"
letter 2 = "G"
letter _ = "T"

unpack k key = if k == 1 then letter key else letter (key / 4) ++ letter (key % 4)

-- Only tables of sizes 4 and 16 are sorted; ties retain ascending base-4 key.
best : IntTable -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO Int
best table limit i winner maximum =
  if i < limit then do
    n <- readIntTable table i
    if maximum < n then best table limit (i + 1) i n else best table limit (i + 1) winner maximum
  else return winner

frequencies : IntTable -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
frequencies table length k limit remaining =
  if remaining == 0 then putStrLn ""
  else do
    key <- best table limit 0 0 0
    n <- readIntTable table key
    if n == 0 then putStrLn ""
    else do
      let frequency = divDouble (mulDouble 100.0 (intToDouble n)) (intToDouble (length - k + 1))
      putStrLn (unpack k key ++ " " ++ formatDouble 3 frequency)
      writeIntTable table key 0
      frequencies table length k limit (remaining - 1)

query : ByteArray -> Int -> String -> IO ()
query bytes length pattern = do
  word <- byteArrayFromString pattern
  k <- lengthByteArray word
  key <- encode word 0 k 0
  table <- count bytes length k
  n <- readIntTable table key
  putStrLn (showInt n ++ "\t" ++ pattern)

main = do
  skip ()
  initial <- newByteArray 1024 0
  buffer <- readSequence initial 0 1024
  case buffer of
    Buffer bytes length capacity -> do
      one <- count bytes length 1
      frequencies one length 1 4 4
      two <- count bytes length 2
      frequencies two length 2 16 16
      query bytes length "GGT"
      query bytes length "GGTA"
      query bytes length "GGTATT"
      query bytes length "GGTATTTTAATT"
      query bytes length "GGTATTTTAATTTATAGT"

-- Scalar z <- z*z+c, with at most 50 iterations per pixel. ByteArray holds
-- one PBM row; no Unicode encoding is applied to its packed bytes.

-- Orbit values are scalar arguments, as in the C recurrence.
pixel : Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Int -> IO Int
pixel zr zi tr ti cr ci remaining =
  if ltDouble 4.0 (addDouble tr ti) then return 0
  else
    if remaining == 0 then return 1
    else
      let
        nextI = addDouble (mulDouble (mulDouble 2.0 zr) zi) ci
        nextR = addDouble (subDouble tr ti) cr
      in pixel nextR nextI (mulDouble nextR nextR) (mulDouble nextI nextI) cr ci (remaining - 1)

-- Interleave two independent scalar orbits. An escaped lane stays masked
-- while its neighbour finishes; no threads or explicit SIMD are involved.
pixels : Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Double -> Bool -> Bool -> Int -> IO Int
pixels zr0 zi0 tr0 ti0 cr0 zr1 zi1 tr1 ti1 cr1 ci active0 active1 remaining =
  let
    live0 = if ltDouble 4.0 (addDouble tr0 ti0) then false else active0
    live1 = if ltDouble 4.0 (addDouble tr1 ti1) then false else active1
  in if live0 || live1 then
    if remaining == 0 then return ((if live0 then 2 else 0) + (if live1 then 1 else 0))
    else
      let
        nextI0 = addDouble (mulDouble (mulDouble 2.0 zr0) zi0) ci
        nextR0 = addDouble (subDouble tr0 ti0) cr0
        nextI1 = addDouble (mulDouble (mulDouble 2.0 zr1) zi1) ci
        nextR1 = addDouble (subDouble tr1 ti1) cr1
      in pixels nextR0 nextI0 (mulDouble nextR0 nextR0) (mulDouble nextI0 nextI0) cr0 nextR1 nextI1 (mulDouble nextR1 nextR1) (mulDouble nextI1 nextI1) cr1 ci live0 live1 (remaining - 1)
  else return 0

pad : ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
pad out index bits =
  if bits == 0 then return ()
  else do
    byte <- readByteArray out index
    writeByteArray out index (byte * 2)
    pad out index (bits - 1)

row : ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
row out n y x =
  if x < n then do
    let cr = subDouble (divDouble (mulDouble 2.0 (intToDouble x)) (intToDouble n)) 1.5

    let index = x / 8

-- Five-body scalar simulation, matching nbody-gcc-1. Each body occupies
-- seven contiguous DoubleArray cells: x,y,z,vx,vy,vz,mass. All integration,
-- pair iteration, momentum correction and energy calculation are MLF code.

solarMass = mulDouble (mulDouble 4.0 3.141592653589793) 3.141592653589793

year = 365.24

get b i field = readDoubleArray b (i + field)

set b i field x = writeDoubleArray b (i + field) x

norm2 x y z = addDouble (addDouble (mulDouble x x) (mulDouble y y)) (mulDouble z z)

initialize : DoubleArray -> IO ()
initialize b = do
  set b 0 6 solarMass
  set b 7 0 4.84143144246472090e+00
  set b 7 1 (-1.16032004402742839e+00)
  set b 7 2 (-1.03622044471123109e-01)
  set b 7 3 (mulDouble 1.66007664274403694e-03 year)
  set b 7 4 (mulDouble 7.69901118419740425e-03 year)
  set b 7 5 (mulDouble (-6.90460016972063023e-05) year)
  set b 7 6 (mulDouble 9.54791938424326609e-04 solarMass)
  set b 14 0 8.34336671824457987e+00
  set b 14 1 4.12479856412430479e+00
  set b 14 2 (-4.03523417114321381e-01)
  set b 14 3 (mulDouble (-2.76742510726862411e-03) year)
  set b 14 4 (mulDouble 4.99852801234917238e-03 year)
  set b 14 5 (mulDouble 2.30417297573763929e-05 year)
  set b 14 6 (mulDouble 2.85885980666130812e-04 solarMass)
  set b 21 0 1.28943695621391310e+01
  set b 21 1 (-1.51111514016986312e+01)
  set b 21 2 (-2.23307578892655734e-01)
  set b 21 3 (mulDouble 2.96460137564761618e-03 year)
  set b 21 4 (mulDouble 2.37847173959480950e-03 year)
  set b 21 5 (mulDouble (-2.96589568540237556e-05) year)
  set b 21 6 (mulDouble 4.36624404335156298e-05 solarMass)
  set b 28 0 1.53796971148509165e+01
  set b 28 1 (-2.59193146099879641e+01)
  set b 28 2 1.79258772950371181e-01
  set b 28 3 (mulDouble 2.68067772490389322e-03 year)
  set b 28 4 (mulDouble 1.62824170038242295e-03 year)
  set b 28 5 (mulDouble (-9.51592254519715870e-05) year)
  set b 28 6 (mulDouble 5.15138902046611451e-05 solarMass)

offset : DoubleArray -> Int -> Double -> Double -> Double -> IO ()

    z <- get b i 2
    m <- get b i 6
    x2 <- get b j 0
    y2 <- get b j 1
    z2 <- get b j 2
    m2 <- get b j 6

    z2 <- get b j 2
    m2 <- get b j 6

    let dy = subDouble y y2
    let dz = subDouble z z2
    let distance = sqrtDouble (norm2 dx dy dz)
    let mag = divDouble 0.01 (mulDouble (mulDouble distance distance) distance)
    vx <- get b i 3
    vy <- get b i 4
    vz <- get b i 5
    vx2 <- get b j 3
    vy2 <- get b j 4
    vz2 <- get b j 5
    set b i 3 (subDouble vx (mulDouble (mulDouble dx m2) mag))
    set b i 4 (subDouble vy (mulDouble (mulDouble dy m2) mag))
    set b i 5 (subDouble vz (mulDouble (mulDouble dz m2) mag))

  if i == 35 then return ()
  else do
    x <- get b i 0
    y <- get b i 1
    z <- get b i 2
    vx <- get b i 3
    vy <- get b i 4
    vz <- get b i 5
    set b i 0 (addDouble x (mulDouble 0.01 vx))
    set b i 1 (addDouble y (mulDouble 0.01 vy))
    set b i 2 (addDouble z (mulDouble 0.01 vz))
    positions b (i + 7)

  if n == 0 then return ()
  else do
    velocities b 0
    positions b 0
    advance b (n - 1)

  before <- energy bodies 0 0.0
  putStrLn (formatDouble 9 before)
  advance bodies (readInt input)
  after <- energy bodies 0 0.0
  putStrLn (formatDouble 9 after)

-- Sequential unbounded spigot: both extract(3) and extract(4) are evaluated.
-- Explicit Integer retains the unbounded arithmetic; loop counters use Int64.
-- Arithmetic uses language primitives, not a foreign pi helper.

spaces : Int -> String
spaces n = if n == 0 then "" else " " ++ spaces (n - 1)

digits : Int -> Int -> Int -> Integer -> Integer -> Integer -> String -> IO ()
digits wanted produced k num acc den row =
  if produced == wanted then
    if produced % 10 == 0 then return ()
    else putStrLn (row ++ spaces (10 - produced % 10) ++ "\t:" ++ showInt produced)
  else
    let
      nextK = k + 1
      twice = nextK * 2 + 1
      n = mulInteger num (intToInteger nextK)
      a = mulInteger (addInteger acc (mulInteger num (intToInteger 2))) (intToInteger twice)
      d = mulInteger den (intToInteger twice)
    in if ltInteger a n then digits wanted produced nextK n a d row
    else
      let
        q = quotInteger (addInteger (mulInteger n (intToInteger 3)) a) d
        r = quotInteger (addInteger (mulInteger n (intToInteger 4)) a) d
      in if eqInteger q r then
        let
          count = produced + 1
          text = row ++ showInteger q
        in do
          if count % 10 == 0 then putStrLn (text ++ "\t:" ++ showInt count) else return ()
          digits wanted count nextK (mulInteger n (intToInteger 10)) (mulInteger (subInteger a (mulInteger d q)) (intToInteger 10)) d (if count % 10 == 0 then "" else text)
      else digits wanted produced nextK n a d row

main = do
  input <- getLine
  digits (readInt input) 0 0 (intToInteger 1) (intToInteger 0) (intToInteger 1) ""

-- Reverse-complement every FASTA record, using a complement lookup table
-- and reusable 60-column output chunks. All byte work is written in MLF.

minimum a b = if a < b then a else b

-- Read one line at a time. Each record starts small and doubles as needed;
-- no file-size query or whole-input allocation is used.
copy : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
copy source dest n offset i =
  if i < n then do
    b <- readByteArray source i
    writeByteArray dest (offset + i) b
    copy source dest n offset (i + 1)
  else return ()

capacityFor : Int -> Int -> IO Int
capacityFor capacity needed = if capacity < needed then capacityFor (capacity * 2) needed else return capacity

trimLine : ByteArray -> Int -> IO Int
trimLine line n =
  if n == 0 then return 0
  else do
    b <- readByteArray line (n - 1)
    if b == 10 then trimLine line (n - 1) else if b == 13 then trimLine line (n - 1) else return n

initTable : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> IO ()
initTable table letters complements i =
  if i < 16 then do
    b <- readByteArray letters i
    c <- readByteArray complements i
    writeByteArray table b c
    writeByteArray table (b + 32) c
    initTable table letters complements (i + 1)
  else return ()

fillRow : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
fillRow table source out last offset count i =
  if i < count then do
    b <- readByteArray source (last - i)
    c <- readByteArray table b
    writeByteArray out (offset + i) c
    fillRow table source out last offset count (i + 1)
  else return ()

fill : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
fill table source out last remaining offset =
  if remaining == 0 then return ()
  else do
    let count = minimum remaining 60
    fillRow table source out last offset count 0
    writeByteArray out (offset + count) 10
    fill table source out (last - count) (remaining - count) (offset + count + 1)

emit : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> IO ()
emit table out source remaining =
  if remaining == 0 then return ()
  else do
    let count = minimum remaining 61440
    fill table source out (remaining - 1) count 0
    putBytes out 0 (count + (count + 59) / 60)
    emit table out source (remaining - count)

records : ByteArray -> ByteArray -> ByteArray -> Int -> Int -> IO ()
records table out bytes used capacity = do
  line <- getByteLine
  length <- lengthByteArray line
  if length == 0 then emit table out bytes used
  else do
    first <- readByteArray line 0
    if first == 62 then do
      emit table out bytes used
      putBytes line 0 length
      records table out bytes 0 capacity
    else do
      count <- trimLine line length
      let needed = used + count
      if capacity < needed then do
        next <- capacityFor capacity needed
        grown <- newByteArray next 0
        copy bytes grown used 0 0
        copy line grown count used 0
        records table out grown needed next
      else do
        copy line bytes count used 0
        records table out bytes needed capacity

main = do
  table <- newByteArray 256 0
  letters <- byteArrayFromString "ACGTUMRWSYKVHDBN"
  complements <- byteArrayFromString "TGCAAKYWSRMBDHVN"
  initTable table letters complements 0
  bytes <- newByteArray 1024 0
  out <- newByteArray 62464 0
  records table out bytes 0 1024

-- Matrix-free power iteration: the same 20 applications of A^T A as the
-- upstream programs. Scalar accumulators are carried between loop iterations.

evalA i j =
  let
    x = intToDouble i
    y = intToDouble j
    sum = addDouble x y
  in divDouble 1.0 (addDouble (addDouble (divDouble (mulDouble sum (addDouble sum 1.0)) 2.0) x) 1.0)

rowA : Int -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> Int -> Int -> Double -> IO ()
rowA n u out i j sum =
  if j < n then do
    x <- readDoubleArray u j
    rowA n u out i (j + 1) (addDouble sum (mulDouble (evalA i j) x))
  else writeDoubleArray out i sum

rowAt : Int -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> Int -> Int -> Double -> IO ()
rowAt n u out i j sum =
  if j < n then do
    x <- readDoubleArray u j
    rowAt n u out i (j + 1) (addDouble sum (mulDouble (evalA j i) x))
  else writeDoubleArray out i sum

evalAv : Int -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> Int -> IO ()
evalAv n u out i =
  if i < n then do
    rowA n u out i 0 0.0
    evalAv n u out (i + 1)
  else return ()

evalAtv : Int -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> Int -> IO ()
evalAtv n u out i =
  if i < n then do
    rowAt n u out i 0 0.0
    evalAtv n u out (i + 1)
  else return ()

evalAtAv n u out tmp = do
  evalAv n u tmp 0
  evalAtv n tmp out 0

power : Int -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> Int -> IO ()
power n u v tmp remaining =
  if remaining == 0 then return ()
  else do
    evalAtAv n u v tmp
    evalAtAv n v u tmp
    power n u v tmp (remaining - 1)

dot : Int -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> DoubleArray -> Int -> IO ()
dot n u v sums i =
  if i < n then do
    x <- readDoubleArray u i
    y <- readDoubleArray v i
    uv <- readDoubleArray sums 0
    vv <- readDoubleArray sums 1
    writeDoubleArray sums 0 (addDouble uv (mulDouble x y))
    writeDoubleArray sums 1 (addDouble vv (mulDouble y y))
    dot n u v sums (i + 1)
  else return ()

main = do
  input <- getLine
  let n = readInt input
  u <- newDoubleArray n 1.0
  v <- newDoubleArray n 0.0
  tmp <- newDoubleArray n 0.0
  sums <- newDoubleArray 2 0.0
  power n u v tmp 10
  dot n u v sums 0
  uv <- readDoubleArray sums 0
  vv <- readDoubleArray sums 1
  putStrLn (formatDouble 9 (sqrtDouble (divDouble uv vv)))
